title: Qur'ānic Examples of أَمَّا and the Future سَـ, then Conjugating the مُضَارِع with لَيْسَ and Negation
summary: The first half reviews homework in which students hunted for Qur'ānic āyāt containing أَمَّا (ammā : as for) and the future prefix سَـ (sa-), with the teacher confirming each example and explaining the vocabulary inside it. The second half moves into the tamrīnāt of lesson eleven: conjugating the مُضَارِع (muḍāriʿ : present tense) verb across persons and genders using ذَهَبَ, the full chart of لَيْسَ (laysa : is not), and the rule that مَا negates the past while لَا negates the present.
key_points: أَمَّا (ammā : as for) sets up a contrast and is answered by a فَ (fa-) on the following clause — فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَهُوَ، وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُمُّهُ.
The prefix سَـ (sa-) attaches to a مُضَارِع (muḍāriʿ : present tense) verb to give future meaning — سَيَقُولُونَ (sa-yaqūlūna : they will say), سَنَسِمُهُ (sa-nasimuhu : We will brand him).
خَفَّتْ (khaffat) comes from خَفِيف (khafīf : light), so مَوَازِينُهُ خَفَّتْ means his scales were light.
وَسَمَ يَسِمُ (wasama / yasimu) means to put a mark on something, which is why سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ means We will brand him on the snout.
لَيْسَ (laysa) must agree with who is being spoken about, not the speaker: لَسْتُ (lastu : I am not) for oneself, but لَيْسَ (laysa) when speaking about ʿAbdullāh.

The مُضَارِع (muḍāriʿ) verb changes prefix by person and gender — يَذْهَبُ (yadhhabu : he goes), تَذْهَبُ (tadhhabu : she goes / you m.s. go), أَذْهَبُ (adhhabu : I go), يَذْهَبُونَ (yadhhabūna : they m. go), يَذْهَبْنَ (yadhhabna : they f. go).
تَذْهَبُ (tadhhabu) is used both for a singular female being spoken about and for a male being spoken to — context decides which.
In إِضَافَة (iḍāfah) the first term drops its tanwīn: فِي مَسْجِدِ حَمْزَةَ (fī masjidi Ḥamzah), never فِي مَسْجِدٍ حَمْزَةَ.
مَا (mā) negates the مَاضِي (māḍī : past) — مَا ذَهَبَ (mā dhahaba : he did not go) — while لَا (lā) negates the مُضَارِع (muḍāriʿ : present) — لَا أَشْرَبُ (lā ashrabu : I do not drink).
The teacher's advice on method: memorise the conjugation chart until applying it becomes second nature, rather than reasoning it out afresh each time.
questions: [00:28:04] Q: Could we use مَا to negate a present-tense verb the way we do with the past? — A: Not yet learned at this point, but مَا is mostly for the past; for the present you use لَا, so لَا أَعْرِفُ is the technically correct way to say I do not know.
[00:31:07] Q: What are those two lines above the exercise? — A: They are just the worked example, so read them to see the pattern before filling in the blanks.
[00:35:02] Q: So would I say يَذْهَبُ to mean I am going? — A: No, يَذْهَبُ means he is going; for yourself you use أَذْهَبُ with the hamza prefix.
[00:42:01] Q: Is أَسْئِلَة the plural of سُؤَال? — A: Yes, أَسْئِلَة (asʾilah : questions) is the plural of سُؤَال (suʾāl : question).
[00:46:00] Q: Does دَفْتَر mean office, as it does in Urdu? — A: No — in Arabic دَفْتَر is a notebook, while مَكْتَب (maktab) is the office or desk.
[00:51:01] Q: Can لَا be used with the present tense? — A: Yes, that is exactly its use: add لَا for the present and مَا for the past.

quiz.q: In the construction أَمَّا … فَـ …, what role does the فَ play?
options: It negates the clause that follows
It introduces the answer clause that completes the أَمَّا contrast
It marks the verb as future tense
It turns the noun into an إِضَافَة
quiz.a: The lecture's examples all pair أَمَّا with a following فَ that carries the answer, as in فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ.

quiz.q: What does the prefix سَـ add to a مُضَارِع verb?
quiz.a: The teacher explained سَـ as the marker of futurity, citing سَيَقُولُونَ (they will say) and سَنَسِمُهُ (We will brand him).

quiz.q: From which root does خَفَّتْ in وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ come, and what does it mean?
quiz.a: The teacher derived خَفَّتْ from خَفِيف (light), so the āyah describes scales that were light.

quiz.q: Speaking about ʿAbdullāh rather than yourself, which form of لَيْسَ is correct?
quiz.a: لَسْتُ is for the speaker; since the sentence is about him, the third-person masculine لَيْسَ is used — the point the teacher made when correcting the student.

quiz.q: Which مُضَارِع form means my sister goes?
quiz.a: A singular female being spoken about takes تَذْهَبُ, as the teacher showed with أُخْتِي تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.

quiz.q: Why is فِي مَسْجِدِ حَمْزَةَ correct rather than فِي مَسْجِدٍ حَمْزَةَ?
options: Because the مُضَاف drops its tanwīn
Because حَمْزَة is a proper noun
Because the preposition فِي forbids tanwīn
quiz.a: The teacher corrected the student on exactly this: as the مُضَاف, مَسْجِد cannot carry tanwīn.

quiz.q: Which particle negates a مَاضِي verb, according to the lesson?
quiz.a: The teacher's rule was مَا for the past — مَا كَتَبَ, مَا ذَهَبَ — and لَا for the present.

quiz.q: How would you negate أَشْرَبُ الشَّايَ to mean I do not drink tea?
quiz.a: Since أَشْرَبُ is مُضَارِع, the negation is لَا — the teacher gave لَا أَشْرَبُ as the model answer for that tamrīn.

quiz.q: What does وَسَمَ يَسِمُ mean, as explained for سَنَسِمُهُ عَلَى الْخُرْطُومِ?
options: To put a mark on something
quiz.a: The teacher glossed وَسَمَ يَسِمُ as putting a mark on something, comparing it to a brand or tattoo.

quiz.q: Which form completes الطَّالِبَاتُ ـــــ الْمَلَابِسَ بِالصَّابُونِ (the female students wash the clothes with soap)?
quiz.a: A third-person feminine plural doer takes the نَ ending — يَغْسِلْنَ — the pattern drilled through these tamrīnāt.

quran_examples.arabic: فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فَيُوَفِّيهِمْ أُجُورَهُمْ وَيَزِيدُهُم مِّن فَضْلِهِ ۖ وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ اسْتَنكَفُوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا فَيُعَذِّبُهُمْ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-ammā alladhīna āmanū wa-ʿamilū al-ṣāliḥāti fa-yuwaffīhim ujūrahum wa-yazīduhum min faḍlih, wa-ammā alladhīna istankafū wa-istakbarū fa-yuʿadhdhibuhum ʿadhāban alīmā
quran_examples.translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full and increase them from His bounty; and as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment.
quran_examples.note: The example a student brought for أَمَّا — it shows the paired أَمَّا … وَأَمَّا contrast, each answered by a فَ.

quran_examples.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَن ثَقُلَتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَهُوَ فِي عِيشَةٍ رَاضِيَةٍ ۝ وَأَمَّا مَنْ خَفَّتْ مَوَازِينُهُ فَأُمُّهُ هَاوِيَةٌ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-ammā man thaqulat mawāzīnuhu fa-huwa fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyah, wa-ammā man khaffat mawāzīnuhu fa-ummuhu hāwiyah
quran_examples.translation: As for the one whose scales are heavy, he will be in a pleasant life; and as for the one whose scales are light, his refuge will be the Fire.
quran_examples.note: Used in class to illustrate أَمَّا and to derive خَفَّتْ from خَفِيف (light).

quran_examples.translation: But as for the unjust, they will be firewood for Hellfire.
quran_examples.note: A student's example from Sūrat al-Jinn, another instance of أَمَّا answered by فَ.

quran_examples.arabic: فَأَمَّا ثَمُودُ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِالطَّاغِيَةِ ۝ وَأَمَّا عَادٌ فَأُهْلِكُوا بِرِيحٍ صَرْصَرٍ عَاتِيَةٍ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-ammā thamūdu fa-uhlikū bi-l-ṭāghiyah, wa-ammā ʿādun fa-uhlikū bi-rīḥin ṣarṣarin ʿātiyah
quran_examples.translation: As for Thamūd, they were destroyed by the overpowering blast; and as for ʿĀd, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind.
quran_examples.note: The āyah the class worked through at the start when recalling how Thamūd and ʿĀd were each destroyed.

quran_examples.arabic: فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-ammā man ūtiya kitābahu bi-yamīnihi fa-sawfa yuḥāsabu ḥisāban yasīrā
quran_examples.translation: As for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will be judged with an easy reckoning.
quran_examples.note: Cited for أَمَّا, and it also carries سَوْفَ — the longer sister of the future prefix سَـ discussed in the same session.

quran_examples.arabic: قُلْ مَّن رَّبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ السَّبْعِ وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ ۝ سَيَقُولُونَ لِلَّهِ
quran_examples.transliteration: qul man rabbu al-samāwāti al-sabʿi wa-rabbu al-ʿarshi al-ʿaẓīm, sa-yaqūlūna li-llāh
quran_examples.translation: Say: Who is Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Great Throne? They will say: Allah.
quran_examples.note: The first example offered for the future prefix: سَيَقُولُونَ (they will say).

quran_examples.translation: And you will remember what I say to you.
quran_examples.note: Discussed as سَـ on تَذْكُرُونَ, with the teacher noting it was spoken by the believer of Fir'awn's family who had concealed his faith.

quran_examples.translation: We will brand him upon the snout.
quran_examples.note: Used both for the future سَـ and to teach the verb وَسَمَ يَسِمُ (to put a mark on something).

quran_examples.arabic: وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنقَلَبٍ يَنقَلِبُونَ
quran_examples.transliteration: wa-sa-yaʿlamu alladhīna ẓalamū ayya munqalabin yanqalibūn
quran_examples.translation: And those who have wronged will come to know to what return they will be returned.
quran_examples.note: Another future-سَـ example raised in the same homework review.
The teacher tied the drill sentence أَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ to this āyah, showing the second-person masculine plural مُضَارِع of ذَهَبَ.
